hypotheses.claim: Emergence evaluation that discovers and scores macro abstractions on the same finite traces is selection-biased and can manufacture apparent macro information under a causal null.
hypotheses.counter: The search bias is negligible at realistic candidate counts/sample sizes.
hypotheses.falsifier: Nested held-out/permutation evaluation shows no systematic same-data inflation under realistic H1 macro candidate search.

hypotheses.claim: A valid FRANK emergent-organ candidate requires a frozen/preregistered macro identity or discovery/evaluation split plus complexity/multiplicity controls before macro causal gain can count as evidence.
hypotheses.counter: Intervention-based EI/PEID alone is sufficient even when macro definitions are adaptively selected on the evaluated traces.
hypotheses.falsifier: Demonstrate a selection-invariant estimator with calibrated nulls under adaptive macro search.

hypotheses.claim: Joint intervention information plus pairwise/single-source controls can expose higher-order synergy that individual source effects miss.
hypotheses.counter: Pairwise effects are sufficient for all relevant FRANK mechanisms.
hypotheses.falsifier: H1 higher-order candidates show no held-out joint causal gain over the best matched pairwise/state-machine reduction.

hypotheses.claim: Observational information-flow/readout metrics require intervention/common-driver controls before causal promotion.
hypotheses.counter: Directed observational measures are sufficient for the targeted FRANK traces.
hypotheses.falsifier: Known common-driver injections never create false positive directed-flow evidence under the chosen estimator/conditioning scheme.

hypotheses.claim: The emerging FRANK evidence ladder should be conjunctive/vectorial rather than scalar: held-out stability, intervention gain, lesion, rescue, re-entry counterfactual, simpler-model failure, OOD transfer, implementation transfer and cost/recovery must remain separately inspectable.
hypotheses.counter: A single calibrated scalar can preserve all decision-relevant distinctions without Goodhart loss.
hypotheses.falsifier: A preregistered scalar reproduces all branch decisions and counterexample discrimination across H1/H2/H3 without hiding failure modes.

counterhypotheses: H0-A: apparent macro gains are compression/selection artifacts rather than system-level causal organization.
H0-B: conventional event-driven or pairwise controllers explain the same outcomes with equal intervention response.
H0-C: recurrence and GWT re-entry are correlated timing artifacts rather than causal contributors.
H0-D: higher-order synergy metrics are estimator artifacts or finite-sample bias.
H0-E: a macro description predicts well but adds no intervention-relevant causal information beyond the microstate.
